title: Is there a future for models in the LLM era?
title_zh: ARTHUR: 通过混合UML推理重构遗留Java代码的多智能体框架

paragraphs.en: In an era where software development is deeply tied with Large Language Models, does Model Driven Engineering (MDE) still make sense? This raises the question of the extent to which MDE can be successfully combined with an LLM approach to address the downsides of each approach separately. In this paper, we try to answer that question by investigating a central Research Question: Can Agents powered by Large Language Models improve code generated from UML diagrams and text specifications by Model Driven Engineering (MDE) tools? To investigate this problem, we developed a novel LLM-powered Multi-Agentic approach called ARTHUR (Architecture Refactoring Through Hybrid UML Reasoning), a framework that aims at combining the reliability of MDE and the ease of use of LLMs. ARTHUR is designed to refactor legacy Java code produced by traditional, rule-based, MDE code generators from UML diagrams. To assess this question, we refactored the legacy code of several projects from our custom dataset crafted for this purpose. ARTHUR made it possible to add support for modern frameworks like Spring Boot, while ensuring compliance with Model-Based Testing techniques to verify that the code still corresponds to the initial model’s specifications. We then measured the results obtained in terms of time and cost, passing test rate, and compile@k , pass@k and pass k metrics. We also observed the effect of generating code directly from the conceptual model without the refactoring. Our preliminary test results show that MDE could not be further from retirement, after all.

paragraphs.en: Model Driven Engineering (MDE) focuses on using models to drive the development of software applications. After its first formalization in 2002 ( Kent, 2002 ) , the approach gained traction and began to be adopted in various real-world industrial contexts, reaching its peak adoption in the early 2010s ( Hutchinson et al., 2011 ) . However, in the years leading up to the 2020s, MDE gradually lost popularity among practitioners, despite remaining a very successful approach when adopted correctly ( Verbruggen and Snoeck, 2023 ) . The reasons for this inversion of trend are numerous and difficult to pinpoint. Surely, one big factor is the shift away from strictly object-oriented programming in favor of script-like programming, as promoted by languages such as JavaScript or Python ( Johri and Bansal, 2018 ) . Nevertheless, we believe that the reason that MDE is no longer the industry standard is its intrinsic complexity. Crafting a good conceptual model from a client’s requirements, is a very hard task, and fewer and fewer professionals are capable of doing so.
paragraphs.zh: 模型驱动工程（MDE）专注于利用模型来指导软件应用的开发。 自 2002 年首次被正式提出（Kent, 2002）以来，这种方法逐渐获得认可，并开始应用于各种实际工业场景，其采用率在 2010 年代初达到顶峰（Hutchinson et al., 2011）。 然而，在 2020 年代之前的几年里，尽管 MDE 在正确应用时仍然是一种非常成功的方法（Verbruggen and Snoeck, 2023），但它却在从业者中逐渐失去了流行度。 导致这一趋势逆转的原因有很多，而且难以准确确定。 毫无疑问，一个重要的因素是编程方式从严格的面向对象编程转向了类似脚本的编程模式，正如 JavaScript 或 Python 等语言所倡导的那样（Johri and Bansal, 2018）。 尽管如此，我们认为 MDE 不再成为行业标准的原因在于其内在的复杂性。 根据客户的要求构建一个良好的概念模型是一项非常困难的任务，而能够完成这项任务的专业人士也日益减少。

paragraphs.en: RQ: Can agents powered by Large Language Models improve code generated from UML diagrams and text specifications by Model Driven Engineering (MDE) approaches and tools?
paragraphs.zh: 研究问题：由大型语言模型驱动的智能体，能否通过模型驱动工程（MDE）方法及相关工具，改进基于UML图和文本规范生成的代码？

paragraphs.en: To investigate this problem, we developed a novel LLM-powered Multi-Agentic approach called ARTHUR (Architecture Refactoring Through Hybrid UML Reasoning), that aims at combining the reliability of MDE and the ease of use of LLMs. ARTHUR receives the system’s textual requirements, the corresponding UML diagrams, and the Java legacy code generated using existing MDE tools as input and aims to leverage LLMs to create modern applications ready to be deployed with new technology stacks, such as Spring Boot and React. The general idea is to investigate to what extent agents maintains the structure and the constraints of the MDE-generated code. Finally, to ensure the rigor of the testing approach, we want to base it on a the Model-Driven Testing (MDT) approach proposed in ( Mussa et al., 2009 ) . This allows to be sure that the generated code is still as compliant to the conceptual as the one crafted by the classic existing MDE tools.
paragraphs.zh: 为了研究这个问题，我们开发了一种基于大型语言模型（LLM）的新型多智能体方法，名为 ARTHUR（通过混合 UML 推理进行架构重构），旨在结合模型驱动工程（MDE）的可靠性和大型语言模型（LLM）的易用性。 ARTHUR 接收系统的文本需求、相应的 UML 图以及使用现有 MDE 工具生成的 Java 遗留代码作为输入，并试图利用大型语言模型（LLM）创建现代化的应用程序，使其能够使用新的技术栈（如 Spring Boot 和 React）进行部署。 其总体思路是研究智能体在多大程度上能够保持由 MDE 生成的代码的结构和约束。 最后，为确保测试方法的严谨性，我们希望基于（Mussa 等人，2009）提出的模型驱动测试（MDT）方法。 这样可以确保生成的代码在概念合规性方面与经典现有 MDE 工具所编写的代码保持一致。

paragraphs.en: For the Model-Driven Engineering (MDE) and Model-Driven Development (MDD) approaches, the standard modeling language of choice was mainly Unified Modeling Language (UML) ( Kent, 2002 ) , for its incredible versatility and support to different kinds of diagrams ( Fowler, 2018 ) . UML has historically been the norm, but modern practices often privilege UML textual representations ( Romeo et al., 2025 ) like PlantUML 1 1 1 https://plantuml.com/guide or its variant, i.e. tUML ( Buchmann et al., 2024 ) . Translating these conceptual architectures into code, to kickstart developers’ tasks, relies on generation toolchains such as the Eclipse Modeling Framework (EMF) 2 2 2 https://eclipse.dev/emf/ or the Merlin Prototyper 3 3 3 https://merode.econ.kuleuven.be/pages/CodeGeneration.html , which transforms UML diagrams into functional Java applications.
paragraphs.zh: 在模型驱动工程（MDE）和模型驱动开发（MDD）方法中，主要选择的标准化建模语言是统一建模语言（UML）（Kent, 2002），这得益于其惊人的灵活性和对各类图表的支持（Fowler, 2018）。 UML 历来是主流标准，但现代实践往往更青睐 UML 的文本化表示形式（Romeo et al., 2025），例如 PlantUML 1 1 1 https://plantuml.com/guide 或其变体 tUML（Buchmann et al., 2024）。 为了启动开发者的任务，将这些概念架构转化为代码需要依赖生成工具链，例如 Eclipse Modeling Framework（EMF）2 2 2 https://eclipse.dev/emf/ 或 Merlin Prototyper 3 3 3 https://merode.econ.kuleuven.be/pages/CodeGeneration.html，它们能将 UML 图表转换为可运行的 Java 应用程序。

paragraphs.en: Recently, a paradigm shift has occurred with the integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) and new agentic modalities. Models such as Claude 4.6, GPT-5, and Kimi 2.5 provide native agentic support capable of complex programming tasks ( Plaat et al., 2025 ) . To rigorously evaluate code generated by these probabilistic models, researchers utilize metrics like pass@k , which measures the frequency of code passing functional tests within k k attempts, alongside compile@k to verify syntactical correctness ( Yu et al., 2025 ) .
paragraphs.zh: 近期，随着大型语言模型（LLM）与新型智能体模态的融合，研究范式发生了转变。 Claude 4.6、GPT-5 和 Kimi 2.5 等模型提供了原生的智能体支持，能够执行复杂的编程任务（Plaat 等人，2025）。 为了严格评估这些概率模型生成的代码，研究人员使用了 pass@k 等指标，该指标衡量代码在 k 次尝试中通过功能测试的频率，并结合 compile@k 来验证语法正确性（Yu 等人，2025）。

paragraphs.en: In two out of the nine selected articles, LLMs are leveraged to improve the code MDE-generated from a simple textual description to perform a single task. In this case the improvement should be merely intended in terms of number of test cases passed, since this is the main metric evaluated in the proposed benchmark datasets. Authors of ( Wan et al., 2025 ) demonstrated the impact of adding a LLM-powered agentic pipeline with two actors: a Designer agent to craft a UML activity diagram corresponding to the textual specification to improve the results of the Coder agent on the pass@1 metric on several benchmark datasets like HumanEval ( Chen et al., 2021 ) . The pass@k metric checks how often code passes tests within k attempts, and is one of the most used metrics used for evaluating the quality of LLM-generated code ( Yu et al., 2025 ) . The authors of ( Han et al., 2024 ) showed that adding requirements, even if generated by LLMs, to the problem description given as input to the LLMs for generating single task code improves the quality of metrics like pass@1 . This makes a single generation of the code more reliable.

paragraphs.en: The majority of works that include conceptual modeling in their code generation pipeline target complex applications and show that adding a rigorous structure to LLMs yields the most benefits. In ( Escobar et al., 2025 ) , the authors show that LLMs models starting from the end of 2024, like Gemini 1.5 4 4 4 https://storage.googleapis.com/deepmind-media/gemini/gemini_v1_5_report.pdf or GPT-4o ( Hurst et al., 2024 ) are capable of almost flawlessly translating UML class diagrams into simple yet functional code that represents almost 100% of the requirements specified in the class diagram (still not achieving a fully functional application). In ( Buchmann et al., 2025 ) , the authors present MoProCo, a Visual Studio Code extension 5 5 5 https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/vscode that enables LLMs to support both creating a conceptual model in tUML ( Buchmann et al., 2024 ) (a more verbose variant of PlantUML) to represent conceptual models as text, and generating the corresponding Java code. They claimed in the article that MoProCo should seamlessly and intuitively assist the software developer with the aid of LLMs, wether they wanted to produce the tUML model, to code the application or to simply prompt the LLMs for more specific requests, while still being at the center of the generation loop. However, no rigorous validation is provided with this tool. In ( Sadik et al., 2024 ) , the authors use the test case of a Unmanned Vehicle Fleet for evaluating the capabilities of GPT-4 in generating both Java and Python code in specific Jade 6 6 6 https://jade-project.gitlab.io/ and Pade 7 7 7 https://pade.readthedocs.io/ frameworks using an MDD approach. The authors add UML class and activity diagrams crafted by experts in the generation context to measure the quality of the outputted code. However they only measured the cyclomatic complexity of the code and manually checked its integrity without aspecific metrics. The XdCodeGen approach for generating Java code with LLMs is presented in ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) . It consists of four phases: requirement analysis, modeling, code generation, and code verification. The first three of these are supported by GPT-3.5, while the testing uses MSVL ( Wang et al., 2017 ) , a custom language designed for testing software. They were able to successfully generate a Java Spring Boot app totaling around 20,000 lines of code that passed the testing stage. However the test was conducted on this task only.
paragraphs.zh: 大多数在代码生成流程中纳入概念建模的研究都针对复杂应用，并表明为大型语言模型（LLM）添加严谨的结构能带来最大的收益。 在 (Escobar et al., 2025) 中，作者指出，从 2024 年底开始的大型语言模型（LLM），如 Gemini 1.5 4 4 4 https://storage.googleapis.com/deepmind-media/gemini/gemini_v1_5_report.pdf 或 GPT-4o (Hurst et al., 2024)，几乎能够完美地将 UML 类图转换为简单但功能完整的代码，这些代码几乎涵盖了类图中指定的全部需求（尽管尚未达到完全功能的应用程序）。 在 (Buchmann et al., 2025) 中，作者介绍了 MoProCo——一个 Visual Studio Code 扩展 5 5 5 https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/vscode，它使大型语言模型（LLM）既能支持使用 tUML (Buchmann et al., 2024)（PlantUML 的一种更冗长的变体）以文本形式表示概念模型，也能生成相应的 Java 代码。 他们在文章中声称，MoProCo 借助大型语言模型（LLM），能够无缝且直观地协助软件开发人员，无论他们希望创建 tUML 模型、编写应用程序代码，还是仅通过提示大型语言模型（LLM）提出更具体的请求，同时始终保持在生成流程的核心位置。 然而，该工具并未提供任何严谨的验证。 在 (Sadik et al., 2024) 中，作者使用无人车车队测试用例，评估了 GPT-4 在特定 Jade 6 6 6 https://jade-project.gitlab.io/ 和 Pade 7 7 7 https://pade.readthedocs.io/ 框架中通过模型驱动开发（MDD）方法生成 Java 和 Python 代码的能力。 作者还在生成过程中加入了由专家设计的 UML 类和活动图，以衡量所生成代码的质量。 然而，他们仅测量了代码的循环复杂度，并通过人工检查其完整性，而没有使用具体的指标。 (Zhao et al., 2024) 提出了使用大型语言模型（LLM）生成 Java 代码的 XdCodeGen 方法。 该方法包含四个阶段：需求分析、建模、代码生成和代码验证。 其中前三个阶段由 GPT-3.5 提供支持，而测试阶段则使用 MSVL (Wang et al., 2017)，这是一种专为软件测试设计的自定义语言。 他们成功生成了一个总计约 20,000 行代码的 Java Spring Boot 应用程序，并通过了测试阶段。 然而，该测试仅针对这一任务进行。

paragraphs.en: The work closest to our research question is ( He et al., 2025 ) . This work proposed the iEcoreGen framework that integrates the Eclipse Modeling Framework (EMF) and LLMs for generating complex software applications. They ran several experiments to add business support to the generated legacy code, tested with a custom dataset. Despite having conducted a rigorous analysis of several approaches and different Language models, the tests were not guided by a Model Driven Testing approach, and there is no capability of supporting different technology stacks or programming languages. In addition most approaches are not open source.

paragraphs.en: Every project in the dataset is characterized by a business case description written in natural text, where all requirement and logic are clearly stated. paragraphs.en: ARTHUR was designed to be easy to use and to generate reliable code using modern technology stacks. Adding support for new language or technology is as simple as writing a prompt to your favorite AI. We chose to target the refactoring of the monolithic legacy Java application with JSwing user interface created by the Merlin prototyper, outputting a modern web-application with a RESTful backend written in Java with Spring Boot and a front-end written in JavaScript with React framework 15 15 15 react.dev support. We decided to adopt a Multi-Agent architecture ( Li et al., 2024 ) , where a agent is a LLM capable of accessing external tools and performing automatically subsequent action. The access to external tools allow ARTHUR to directly interact with the legacy code generated by the Merlin Prototyper by reading and writing files and directly extracting needed information. ARTHUR’s tools also support terminal commands execution for compiling and debugging the application. The other major advantage of the multi-agent paradigm is the divide et impera built-in approach for every step of the refactoring: the agents do not attempt to create the whole application in one pass, but rather break down the task into smaller sub-tasks --like identifying the classes to implement or making sure the application will compile. This allows ARTHUR to be more reliable than simply prompting your favorite AI in the chat. ARTHUR was built using the OpenHands SDK 16 16 16 https://docs.openhands.dev/sdk Python library. We decided to build the framework with three LLM main agents: i) a Backend Agent, ii) a Front-end Agent, iii) a Test Execution Agent. Before acting, each of the main agents puts down a to-do list with goals to achieve based on the prompt and is allowed to spawn up to 10 sub-agents to perform simpler tasks off the to-do list. The overall architecture is presented in Figure 3 . As the name suggests, each agent will specifically generate a section of the complete architecture. In particular, the test execution agent will extract the tests generated by TesCaV hard-coded into the final Merlin Prototyper output, adapt them for the new application, execute them and write a report with the number of test passed, failed and skipped. sents.en: ARTHUR was designed to be easy to use and to generate reliable code using modern technology stacks.
sents.zh: ARTHUR 的设计旨在易于使用，并能利用现代技术栈生成可靠的代码。

sents.en: Adding support for new language or technology is as simple as writing a prompt to your favorite AI.
sents.zh: 添加对新语言或技术的支持，只需像向你最喜爱的 AI 写入提示那样简单。

sents.en: We chose to target the refactoring of the monolithic legacy Java application with JSwing user interface created by the Merlin prototyper, outputting a modern web-application with a RESTful backend written in Java with Spring Boot and a front-end written in JavaScript with React framework 15 15 15 react.dev support.
sents.zh: 我们选择对由 Merlin 原型设计器创建的、带有 JSwing 用户界面的单体遗留 Java 应用程序进行重构，最终生成一个现代化的 Web 应用程序：其 RESTful 后端使用 Java 和 Spring Boot 编写，前端则使用 JavaScript 和 React framework 15 15 15 react.dev 支持编写。

sents.en: We decided to adopt a Multi-Agent architecture ( Li et al., 2024 ) , where a agent is a LLM capable of accessing external tools and performing automatically subsequent action.
sents.zh: 我们决定采用多智能体架构（Li et al., 2024），其中每个智能体都是一个能够访问外部工具并自动执行后续操作的 LLM。

sents.en: The access to external tools allow ARTHUR to directly interact with the legacy code generated by the Merlin Prototyper by reading and writing files and directly extracting needed information.
sents.zh: 对外部工具的访问使 ARTHUR 能够通过读取和写入文件、直接提取所需信息，与 Merlin 原型设计器生成的遗留代码进行直接交互。

sents.en: ARTHUR’s tools also support terminal commands execution for compiling and debugging the application.
sents.zh: ARTHUR 的工具还支持执行终端命令，用于编译和调试应用程序。

sents.en: The other major advantage of the multi-agent paradigm is the divide et impera built-in approach for every step of the refactoring: the agents do not attempt to create the whole application in one pass, but rather break down the task into smaller sub-tasks --like identifying the classes to implement or making sure the application will compile.
sents.zh: 多智能体范式的另一大优势是，它在重构的每一步都内置了“分而治之”的方法：智能体不会试图一次性创建整个应用程序，而是将任务分解为更小的子任务——例如确定需要实现的类，或确保应用程序能够成功编译。

sents.en: This allows ARTHUR to be more reliable than simply prompting your favorite AI in the chat.
sents.zh: 这使得 ARTHUR 比单纯在聊天中向你最喜爱的 AI 发出提示更为可靠。

sents.en: ARTHUR was built using the OpenHands SDK 16 16 16 https://docs.openhands.dev/sdk Python library.
sents.zh: ARTHUR 是使用 OpenHands SDK 16 16 16 https://docs.openhands.dev/sdk Python 库构建的。

sents.en: Before acting, each of the main agents puts down a to-do list with goals to achieve based on the prompt and is allowed to spawn up to 10 sub-agents to perform simpler tasks off the to-do list.

paragraphs.en: Where n n is the number of tests, c c is the number of successful tests, and k k is indicates how many generation attempts to evaluate. In our testing, compile@k offers the estimated probability of a project refactored by ARTHUR compiling after k k generation attempts (of the same project); pass@k offers the estimated probability of a project to be 100% compliant in relation to the TesCaV tests after k k generation attempts (of the same project); pass k offers the estimated probability of all the k k generations of a project to be 100% compliant in relation to the TesCaV tests after k k generation attempts (of a projects). Those metrics aim at estimating the correctness of a probabilistic generation approach like the ones powered by LLMs, where results of a single run could be not exactly reproducible. However, since the standard pass@k metric computed at a project level does not tell the whole story about the quality of the generation –since it would count as failed even a project with 99% passing test rate, we computed pass@k for the single unit test from TesCaV, computing the estimated probability of passing a single test in k k generation attempt of the same projects, offering a much finer granularity.

paragraphs.en: Following the encouraging yet expensive results of the pilot run, we decided to optimize our initial naïve approach by adding a more efficient LLM as a base for our agents, to make the architecture more effective in terms of price to performance ratio. paragraphs.en: The quick answer to RQ1 is: "yes". First of all, we have observed that changing the LLM powering the agents heavily influences the outcome and even the success of the generation of new code. In our tests, we have observed that smaller LLMs like Codestral 2 are still not capable of fully handling the complexity of the task. At the same time, flagship LLMs like Claude 4.6 Sonnet handle the job almost perfectly, but become hefty in terms of time and money required to complete the generation.

paragraphs.en: The short answer once again is: "pretty good, in a limited sample testing", but, to answer RQ2 properly, we need to contextualize the performance of ARTHUR with respect to the existing literature. In particular, since we have tested the pass@k metrics both in terms of full application compliance and single test compliance, we will compare our results first with iEcoreGen ( He et al., 2025 ) , which measured pass@k and compile@k metrics with respect to the full application; and second with ( Wan et al., 2025 ) and ( Han et al., 2024 ) , which tested their approach on a single function or task, defined in a dataset like HumanEval. Because of being made across different datasets, this kind of comparison is not intended as strict, but rather to position ARTHUR in the flourishing landscape of AI-powered MDE tools. The best performance obtained by iEcoreGen in ( He et al., 2025 ) , are pass@1 =75% and pass@3 =89%, while compile@1 =100% and compile@3 =100%. ARTHUR matched the perfect score on compile@k metrics, falls comparatively short in pass@1 for all three runs, but achieved better results in the first run in the pass@3 metric. The performance gap of 10% (compared to our test run) and more can be partially explained by the different testing approach: as TesCaV ensures full model coverage, the average number of tests per case is more than three times higher (100 compared to 30), increasing the probability of failing a test. On the other hand, the smaller dataset of 8 cases compared to the 20 cases in iEcoreGen also contributes to penalizing our results as not a single app passed 100% of the test cases. Since we felt that the pass metric in at application level was only partially describing ARTHUR’s capabilities, we decided also to measure the pass@k for the single test case. This approach was also followed in ( Wan et al., 2025 ) , where pass@1 was around 95%, and in ARCHCODE ( Han et al., 2024 ) , where respectively pass@1 ,3,5= 86.36% 88.62% 90.48%. These more refined numbers suggest that Run 1 results were above the current literature, Run 2 result, despite the low pass@1 were better as well, but more interestingly, Run 3 results, the ones without using the legacy code as input, were better as well. The explanation for this counterintuitive result, where conceptual model-only code generation was more successful than legacy code refactoring, has to be found in the structure of the conceptual model. We will discuss this in detail the next section.
paragraphs.zh: 简短的回答仍然是：“在有限的样本测试中表现相当不错”，但要恰当地回答研究问题2（RQ2），我们需要将 ARTHUR 的性能置于现有文献的背景下进行说明。 具体来说，由于我们已从完整应用程序合规性和单个测试合规性两个角度测试了 pass@k 指标，因此我们将首先将结果与 iEcoreGen（He et al., 2025）进行比较——该研究测量了针对完整应用程序的 pass@k 和 compile@k 指标；其次再与（Wan et al., 2025）和（Han et al., 2024）进行比较——这两项研究在 HumanEval 等数据集中定义的单个函数或任务上测试了其方法。 由于这些比较跨越了不同的数据集，因此这种比较并非严格意义上的对比，而是旨在将 ARTHUR 置于蓬勃发展的 AI 驱动 MDE 工具领域中定位。 （He et al., 2025）中 iEcoreGen 获得的最高性能为 pass@1 =75% 和 pass@3 =89%，而 compile@1 =100% 和 compile@3 =100%。 ARTHUR 在 compile@k 指标上达到了满分，但在所有三次运行中，其 pass@1 表现相对逊色；不过，在第一次运行中，其在 pass@3 指标上取得了更好的结果。 与我们的测试运行相比，10% 甚至更大的性能差距可以部分归因于不同的测试方法：由于 TesCaV 确保了模型的全覆盖，每个用例的平均测试数量超过三倍（100 次对比 30 次），从而增加了测试失败的概率。 另一方面，与 iEcoreGen 使用的 20 个用例相比，我们仅使用了 8 个用例的较小数据集，这也导致我们的结果受到一定影响，因为没有任何一个应用程序通过了全部 100% 的测试用例。 由于我们认为应用程序级别的 pass 指标仅部分反映了 ARTHUR 的能力，因此我们还决定测量单个测试用例的 pass@k 值。 （Wan et al., 2025）也采用了这种方法，其中 pass@1 约为 95%；而在 ARCHCODE（Han et al., 2024）中，pass@1、3、5 分别达到 86.36%、88.62% 和 90.48%。 这些更精细的数据表明：第一次运行的结果优于当前文献水平；第二次运行尽管 pass@1 较低，但表现同样更佳；更有意义的是，第三次运行（未使用遗留代码作为输入）的结果也同样出色。 这一反直觉结果的解释——即仅基于概念模型生成代码比重构遗留代码更为成功——必须从概念模型的结构中寻找答案。 我们将在下一节详细讨论这一点。

paragraphs.en: A quantitative answer to RQ3 could be: "using the conceptual model as input to ARTHUR led to about 10% more test passed per project in average", but we need to elaborate it more. The most interesting takeaway from our experiment runs is that even with the less powerful LLMs powering ARTHUR and with the input of the conceptual model without the Merlin generated code, we were able to achieve similar and in some cases even better results than the Run 2 that could use the full legacy code base as a reference. This result can be partially explained by the XML format of the conceptual models (See Code 1 ): the XML file clearly states the various part that are going to be tested with TesCaV, like attributes, object states, events and methods. But if the legacy code is equivalent to the model how come the TesCaV results are so different between Run 2 and 3? Our empirical explanation is that, while Merlin-generated code still has all the elements necessary to pass tests, they are diluted in a vast legacy code base, and thus the less powerful llms like Codestral or even Kimi K2.5 do not manage to capture all those elements perfectly.

sents.zh: 我们的经验性解释是：尽管Merlin生成的代码仍然包含通过测试所需的所有元素，但这些元素被分散在庞大的遗留代码库中，因此像Codestral或甚至Kimi K2.5这类能力较弱的LLM无法完美地捕捉到所有这些元素。

paragraphs.en: These results suggest that conceptual modeling could still be crucial in a faster evolving coding landscape where the speed and apparently flawless generation of LLMs are dominant. Our experiments proved that the use of a conceptual model could be more effective for generating code compliant to the specifications instead of prompting it to refactor the legacy code base, as can be done in tools such as Visual Studio Code or Cursor.
paragraphs.zh: 这些结果表明，在 LLM 的速度和看似完美的生成能力占据主导的、发展更快的编码环境中，概念建模可能仍然至关重要。 我们的实验证明，使用概念模型来生成符合规范的代码可能比提示其重构遗留代码库（如 Visual Studio Code 或 Cursor 等工具中所做的那样）更为有效。

paragraphs.en: While the ARTHUR framework demonstrates promising results, several limitations and threats to validity must be acknowledged. First, it is necessary to acknowledge that the agentic loop after having observed too much test failures attempts to fix the code and perform again a sequential testing phase. This paper only reports only the final results, as the intermediate test results could underestimate the capability of the framework that showed an unexpected positive behavior. However, while this iterative refinement improves the final output, it introduces the risk that the agent might over-optimize for specific test cases rather than addressing broader architectural flaws. Second, we observed slightly different numbers of unit tests for a single case across our evaluations due to differences in the generated architecture. Transitioning from a monolithic Java legacy system to a decoupled Spring Boot and React stack inherently alters the application’s structure, making a perfect one-to-one mapping of unit tests challenging and potentially skewing comparative pass rates. Finally, the success of the generation pipeline is heavily dependent on the input quality; a well-done conceptual model is needed to achieve high reliability. Furthermore, our current evaluation is limited because we have a small set of test cases. Validating the framework on only eight projects restricts the immediate generalizability of our findings to more extensive, industrial-scale applications.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管 ARTHUR 框架展现出令人鼓舞的结果，但仍需承认其存在若干局限性以及对有效性的威胁。 首先，必须指出的是，当智能体循环观察到过多的测试失败后，它会尝试修复代码，并再次执行顺序测试阶段。 本文仅报告最终结果，因为中间测试结果可能会低估该框架的能力，因为它表现出了一种出人意料的积极行为。 然而，尽管这种迭代优化能改进最终输出，但也带来了风险：智能体可能会过度针对特定测试用例进行优化，而非解决更广泛的架构缺陷。 其次，由于生成的架构存在差异，我们在不同评估中观察到单个案例的单元测试数量略有不同。 从单体 Java 遗留系统转向解耦的 Spring Boot 和 React 技术栈，本质上会改变应用程序的结构，这使得单元测试的一一对应变得困难，并可能影响比较通过率。 最后，生成流程的成功在很大程度上取决于输入质量；要实现高可靠性，需要一个精心设计的概念模型。 此外，我们当前的评估存在局限性，因为我们使用的测试用例数量较少。 仅在八个项目上验证该框架，使得我们的研究结果在更广泛、工业规模的应用中的即时普适性受到限制。

paragraphs.en: In conclusion, this paper introduces ARTHUR, a novel multi-agent framework that successfully bridges the gap between Model-Driven Engineering (MDE) and Large Language Models (LLMs). By leveraging conceptual models and legacy code, ARTHUR can refactor outdated architectures into modern technology stacks while maintaining almost complete alignment with original system requirements. Our findings indicate that providing LLM agents with rigorous conceptual models significantly enhances the reliability, cost-effectiveness, and speed of code generation compared to relying on legacy code alone.
paragraphs.zh: 总之，本文介绍了 ARTHUR——一种新颖的多智能体框架，它成功弥合了模型驱动工程（MDE）与大型语言模型（LLM）之间的鸿沟。 通过利用概念模型和遗留代码，ARTHUR 能够将过时的架构重构为现代技术栈，同时几乎完全保持与原始系统需求的一致性。 我们的研究结果表明，与仅依赖遗留代码相比，为 LLM 智能体提供严谨的概念模型能显著提升代码生成的可靠性、成本效益和速度。

paragraphs.en: To address current limitations and further validate our approach, our future work will focus on two primary directions. First, we plan to evaluate ARTHUR on a bigger dataset. Expanding our testing to encompass a wider array of complex, real-world MDE projects will help solidify our confidence in the framework’s scalability and robustness. Second, we aim to extend ARTHUR’s agentic capabilities to support Python/Flask or other languages and frameworks. Because the architecture is prompt-driven, adding support for alternative backend and front-end stacks will demonstrate its true language-agnostic potential in modern software engineering.
paragraphs.zh: 为了应对当前的局限性并进一步验证我们的方法，我们未来的工作将聚焦于两个主要方向。 首先，我们计划在一个更大的数据集上评估 ARTHUR。 将测试范围扩大到涵盖更多样、更复杂的真实世界 MDE 项目，将有助于增强我们对该框架可扩展性和稳健性的信心。 其次，我们的目标是扩展 ARTHUR 的智能体能力，以支持 Python/Flask 或其他语言和框架。 由于该架构是提示驱动的，因此增加对替代后端和前端技术栈的支持，将展示其在现代软件工程领域真正的语言无关潜力。
